record.original_question: Characterize exactly when the product of a P-space and an F-space is again an F-space.

evidence.quote: Question 10. Find a characterization for when the product of a P-space and an F-space is again an F-space.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Work in the category of completely regular Hausdorff topological spaces. Recall the following definitions:

- A space X is called a P-space if every G_δ subset of X is open; equivalently, every point of X is a P-point (a point at which every countable intersection of neighborhoods is again a neighborhood).
- A space Y is called an F-space if every cozero set of Y is C*-embedded in Y; equivalently, any two disjoint cozero subsets of Y have disjoint closures.

Problem: Give a necessary and sufficient condition on a P-space X and an F-space Y under which the product space X × Y (with the usual product topology) is again an F-space.
artifact.status_search_result: Partial results exist: Comfort, Hindman and Negrepontis (1969) gave sufficient conditions and characterized those F-spaces whose product with each P-space having a unique non-isolated point is an F-space; later work by Dow on F-spaces and F'-spaces, and recent work on "PF-spaces" (2021), continues to address related sufficient conditions. However, no complete characterization for the general product of a P-space and an F-space appears to have been established, so the problem appears still open in its full generality.

status_evidence.title: F'-spaces and their product with P-spaces (Comfort, Hindman, Negrepontis)
status_evidence.snippet: The principal result gives a sufficient condition that a product space be an F'-space and shows that the condition is, in a strong sense, best possible.
status_evidence.claim: Only sufficient (not fully characterizing) conditions are known for products of P-spaces and F-spaces.

status_evidence.title: On F-spaces and F'-spaces (Dow)
status_evidence.snippet: Hindman's condition provides a characterization of those F-spaces whose product with each P-space with a unique non-isolated point is an F-space.
status_evidence.claim: A characterization is known only in the restricted case of P-spaces with a unique non-isolated point.

status_evidence.title: On PF-spaces (2021)
status_evidence.snippet: PF-spaces are precisely F-spaces in which all but at most one point is a P-point.
status_evidence.claim: Research on the interplay between P-spaces and F-spaces in products continues into the 2020s, indicating the general characterization problem remains active.
